MAX_LEGS().notice: Real products are 2-3 legs (bond/cash, DvP triangles). Caps `legs.length` so propose() can't let a proposer size a trade such that every later accept()/cancel()/ recordLeg() call (each an O(legs.length) scan) becomes disproportionately expensive for the other parties (solidity-auditor fix, 2026-10-05, agents 4/6 FINDING "unbounded-array-gas-dos"/"unbounded-array-gas-griefing").

accept(string).notice: The named counterparty -- any leg party who is NOT the proposer.

bi().notice: BI's own address (the individual signing identity, not the group address) -- resolved the same way BondTracker's `_custodian`/`_issuer` are: a constructor argument, a snapshot from deploy time (a private Pente contract cannot read base-ledger state to discover this some other way).

cancel(string).notice: Any party in legs[], or BI. Only while PROPOSED/ACCEPTED/LEGS_PREPARED -- never after ATOM_CREATED. This call is PURELY AN ATTESTATION for visibility -- it never moves or releases any funds itself, on any path, because this contract is never the spender of a Noto lock (Noto's cancelLock/spendLock are onlySpender-gated; only the actual delegate -- the trade atom -- can ever call them once a lock is delegated). This is actually safe now, REORDERED (lead decision, 2026-10-05; not a contract change): recordAtom runs right after BI builds the atom off-chain, BEFORE any leg delegates (see its own doc comment). So by construction, no leg can EVER be delegated while this function is reachable -- every delegation happens strictly inside ATOM_CREATED, where this function is already unreachable (reverts WrongState). The audit originally flagged a FALSE premise here ("no leg has been delegated yet" was claimed while the OLD design still let delegation happen before recordAtom) -- fixed by changing the required ORDER, not this function, per the lead's explicit decision not to add a new release path here. If a caller ever violates the required order (delegates before recordAtom), this function still cannot release that leg -- there would be no way for this contract to discover an atom address that was never recorded. Don't rely on this function for fund safety; rely on the order (delegateLock's own doc comment in paladin-client documents the client-side rule).

confirmSettled(string).notice: BI only -- an attestation, not an on-chain read (a private contract cannot read the public RestrictedAtom's status). BI calls this after observing AtomStatusChanged(Executed) via its own blockchain event listener.

markFailed(string).notice: BI only -- an attestation, called after BI (or any party) has already cancelled the underlying RestrictedAtom (which releases any delegated legs back to their owners, see RestrictedAtom.cancel()'s own doc comment) and observed it did not execute.

propose(string,bytes32,(address,address,.notice: Called by the initiating bank (whichever party's user starts the negotiation). `tradeId` must be fresh (never proposed before on this contract). Audit fix (solidity-auditor, agent 9 FINDING "missing-caller-authorization"): the caller must be one of the legs' own `from`/`to` -- unlike every other mutator here, this had no such check, letting any privacy-group member squat a tradeId with bogus/empty legs and permanently deny the real trade (CANCELLED, not NONE, is cancel()'s only exit, and an empty-legs trade can never even reach CANCELLED by anyone but BI, since `_isLegParty` is vacuously false for every address). This check also closes that empty-legs case, since no address can be "a party" of zero legs.

recordAtom(string,address).notice: BI only. REORDERED (lead decision, 2026-10-05, closes the cancel() gap below without a new contract function): this now runs right after BI builds the atom off-chain, BEFORE any leg delegates to it. BI must have already called paladin-client's verifyCancelCall for every leg (cancelCall needs no delegation precondition -- see its own doc comment: it only ever returns a leg's OWN funds to its OWN owner). This contract cannot enforce that call itself (a Pente private contract cannot read Noto's state store, a different domain) -- it only records the atom address BI already built. verifyDelegatedLeg is NOT a precondition here; it runs later, per leg, right after that leg actually delegates (using this recorded atomAddress as the delegation target) and before executeAtom, since unlockCall moves funds to the counterparty and still needs the delegation-gated guarantee (the #5b binding rule, LockImmutable).

recordLeg(string,uint256,bytes32,bytes32.notice: Only the bank whose address equals `legs[legIndex].from` may record that leg, and only once (audit fix below). Once every leg has a non-empty `preparedStateId`, state advances to LEGS_PREPARED. Audit fix (solidity-auditor, 12-agent pass, 2026-10-05 -- 6 of 12 agents independently converged on this exact bug): the state guard used to accept `LEGS_PREPARED` as well as `ACCEPTED`. Since state only ever BECOMES LEGS_PREPARED once every leg already has a non-zero `preparedStateId` (see the loop below), that branch could only ever be reached to let a leg owner OVERWRITE an already-prepared leg -- never to complete a pending one. Concretely: with state==LEGS_PREPARED, a leg owner could call this again with `preparedStateId=bytes32(0)`, which made `allPrepared` recompute false -- but the one-way `if (allPrepared) { state = LEGS_PREPARED; }` never had an `else`, so `state` stayed LEGS_PREPARED while a leg was actually unprepared, silently invalidating whatever BI had already read+verified (verifyDelegatedLeg/verifyCancelCall) for that leg before building the trade atom. Fixed by narrowing the guard to ACCEPTED only (a leg can never be recorded a second time, by construction) and, defense-in-depth, an explicit one-shot check in case any future change reopens the state guard.
